design_decisions: The library owns the grammar; the command owns the contract. Widget types, per-category child-count rules, property names and their JSON types stay in FWidgetClassRegistry and FWidgetBlueprintValidator. BuildWidgetJson adds the /Game/MCPGenerated/ limit, a ValidateWidgetJSON pass before anything is touched, the create-versus-rebuild decision, and the read-back. Nothing about UMG was reimplemented.

The response is read back from the built asset, not echoed from the request. DescribeWidget walks the live UWidgetTree from RootWidget through UPanelWidget::GetChildAt, and for a UCanvasPanelSlot reports position and size out of LayoutData.Offsets plus GetZOrder(). Slot layout is applied by a different code path than widget construction, so a tree built with every slot silently at the origin would otherwise read as a success.

A widget tree converges as a whole, not per widget. Components and variables have stable names to merge against; a widget tree has no identity that survives a caller renaming or reordering a node, so a rerun replaces the tree of the asset already at that path. Hence the destructiveIdempotent annotation and a description that says so, rather than a merge that would quietly drop widgets.

BuildWidgetFromJSON refuses a path that already holds an asset, by design, so the existing-asset case routes to RebuildWidgetFromJSON rather than retrying. Creation saves inside the library; Rebuild deliberately does not, so the command saves that path itself and skips the save when the tree did not compile.

The MCP schema is recursive through z.lazy, and zod-to-json-schema terminates the recursion with $ref "#/properties/tree/properties/root/properties/children/items". 4711 bytes of schema, valid JSON Schema, no definitions block. A flat 'tree is an object' schema would have pushed every type error to the far end of a pipe round trip.
api_verification: UWidgetBlueprintFactory through FAssetToolsModule::CreateAsset is the 4.27 creation path the spec called for and works unchanged.
FKismetEditorUtilities::CompileBlueprint compiles a UWidgetBlueprint with no special casing; WidgetBlueprint->Status is checked against BS_UpToDate.

FAnchorData::Offsets is an FMargin and LayoutData is public (CanvasPanelSlot.h:26, :74); UCanvasPanelSlot::GetZOrder() is const (line 153). SetPosition writes Offsets.Left/Top and SetSize writes Offsets.Right/Bottom under a point anchor, which is what the read-back reports.

walls: A graph connection that cannot be resolved is a log line, not an error. The first BP_ProbeDoorV3 build wired brSnd.exec -> playing.exec and playing.exec -> printS.exec, both were dropped with 'Could not resolve pins for connection', and the command still answered compile_status UpToDate, errors [], saved true, connection_count 34. connection_count is the requested count, not the made count. Found by reading log_output, not by anything in the response. New limitation 20.

The cause of that: UAudioComponent::IsPlaying is declared UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable) but is const, and UHT promotes a const BlueprintCallable function with a return value to FUNC_BlueprintPure, so it has no exec pins. Same for UWidget::GetCachedGeometry. Read the declaration for const, not for the macro. New limitation 21.

UWidgetBlueprintLibrary::Create carries meta=(BlueprintInternalUseOnly="true"), which was expected to block a raw CallFunction node. It does not: that metadata only makes UEdGraphSchema_K2::CanUserKismetCallFunction answer false and keep the function out of the palette. A node built with SetFromFunction compiles UpToDate and runs. This saved a second C++ cycle to advertise the registry's CreateWidget factory. New limitation 22.
No PIE screenshot exists, so 'the HUD is on screen' can only be a number. Limitation 14 stands and shaped both proofs in this chunk, exactly as it shaped the door's.

One probe labelled 'reject: unknown slot key' used 'position', which is a legitimate slot key, so it built successfully and left /Game/MCPGenerated/WBP_ProbeReject behind. That asset is a probe artefact, not evidence of a validation hole; the genuine eight-case rejection sweep ran against WBP_ProbeReject2 and left nothing.

notes: The most expensive assumption in this chunk was free to check and nobody had checked it: a spec said 'implementation not started' and 1840 lines of implementation were sitting in the module, compiled, for months. The plan inherited the claim. Reading WidgetClassRegistry.cpp took two minutes and turned a from-scratch UMG builder into a 156-line front.

Both halves of F3 ended up proving themselves the same way the door did, and for the same reason: no runtime property read and no screenshot during PIE, so the graph has to report its own state. The pattern generalises - find the call that returns a handle rather than the one that returns void, then have the handle answer a question in the log.
Every widget_build save logs 'Unable to Check Out From Source Control' as an auto-dismissed modal, exactly as blueprint_build does; the save succeeds.
